lines.text: This Standard Reference Material (SRM) consists of five different phases. The phases, separately bottled, are a-Al2O3
(corundum structure), ZnO (wurtzite structure), TiO (rutile structure), Cr203 (corundum structure), and CeO (fluorite
structure). These phases can be used as internal standards for quantitative analysis and as external standards for check-
ing the intensity response of x-ray diffraction instruments. The five phases cover the range of linear absorption co-
• for CuKa radiation. The intensity values are for a constant diffracting volume (fixed
divergent slit and infinitely thick mounting or equivalent).
The certified relative intensity values (CuK a radiation), for the major diffraction lines below 70° 2(0), for each phase are
given in Table 1. The certified reference intensity ratios (I/Ic) for ZnO, TiOz, Cr203, and CeO, relative to a-Al203 and
the lattice parameters are given in Tables 2 and 3. The uncertainties of the relative intensity and lattice parameter values
are the standard deviations derived from multiple measurements. The uncertainties of the reference intensity ratio values
were determined from the value of the internal inconsistency derived from all possible binary mixtures.
The average crystallite size for each of the five phases is near 2.0 um. Crystallite size broadening of the diffraction peaks
is small but present. This is particularly apparent for a-Al203, which has a nominal crystallite size less than 1.0 um. The
lattice parameters, uncorrected for refraction, were determined with a relative uncertainty of about three parts in 10*
using an internal standard. This uncertainty in the lattice parameter must be increased by a factor of two or three if one
wishes to determine absolute d-spacings as the uncertainties due to the internal standard 20's and to thermal expansion
